input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import subprocess, sys

# Get stage 2 (upstream/main) content
s2 = subprocess.check_output(
    ['git', 'show', ':2:Makefile'], text=True
)
# Get stage 3 (feature branch) content
s3 = subprocess.check_output(
    ['git', 'show', ':3:Makefile'], text=True
)

# The conflict is only in the first few lines (PHONY declaration).
# Strategy: take Stage 2 (upstream) as base, then add
# 'test-review-and-fix-step5-starting-round' to the secondary PHONY line
# if feature branch had it there and upstream didn't.

s2_lines = s2.splitlines(keepends=True)
s3_lines = s3.splitlines(keepends=True)

# Find what feature branch added to the secondary PHONY line
# Stage 3 secondary line (after the big PHONY): .PHONY: test-lib-vote-tally test-findings-classification test-review-and-fix-step5-starting-round
# Stage 2 secondary line: .PHONY: test-lib-vote-tally test-findings-classification
# The new target is: test-review-and-fix-step5-starting-round

TARGET = 'test-review-and-fix-step5-starting-round'

# Build resolution: take Stage 2 as base
resolved_lines = list(s2_lines)

# Find the secondary PHONY line in Stage 2 and add the new target from Stage 3
for i, line in enumerate(resolved_lines):
    stripped = line.rstrip('\n')
    if stripped == '.PHONY: test-lib-vote-tally test-findings-classification':
        resolved_lines[i] = stripped + ' ' + TARGET + '\n'
        print(f"  Applied: added {TARGET} to line {i+1}", file=sys.stderr)
        break

with open('Makefile', 'w') as f:
    f.writelines(resolved_lines)

print("Makefile resolved successfully", file=sys.stderr)
